lesson.title: Living or Non-Living? Sorting Things Around Us
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: You've learned what plants and animals need to survive. Today we'll use that knowledge to answer a tricky question: how can you tell if something is alive at all?

Living things need food or water, grow and change, and can make more of their own kind. Non-living things don't need any of that — a rock doesn't need water, a toy car doesn't grow. Look around your room and pick five things. For each one, ask: does it need food or water? Does it grow? Sort your five things into a 'living' pile and a 'non-living' pile.
You just used real scientific thinking to sort living and non-living things! This week you've learned a lot about what makes something alive.

objectives: Identify the key traits of living things (need food/water, grow and change, can reproduce)
Sort a set of real, familiar objects into living and non-living categories using those traits
materialsNeeded: 5-10 small household objects and/or a houseplant/pet for a real sorting activity
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child: how do you know something is alive? Let them guess before introducing the traits.
2. Introduce the three traits: needs food/water, grows and changes, can make more of its own kind.
3. Gather 5-10 real objects (some living like a plant, some non-living like a toy) and sort them together, testing each against the three traits.
4. Discuss any tricky examples (a stuffed animal looks alive but isn't; a seed doesn't look alive but is).
5. Move to the worksheet: sort the pictured items into living and non-living.
6. Close by finding one more living and one more non-living thing in the room.
differentiationTips: Struggling: start with very clear-cut examples (a rock vs. a dog) before tackling tricky ones like a stuffed animal or a seed
Ready for more: discuss why a fire or a cloud might seem 'alive' (they move and change) but aren't — they don't need food or make more of their own kind
For a hands-on learner, do a real sorting activity with household objects rather than just the worksheet
teacherGuide.answerKey: Sample worksheet sorting: Living — dog, tree, person, flower. Non-living — rock, toy car, chair, book.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Distinguishing living from non-living things using observable evidence is a foundational Kindergarten life-science skill that ties together this week's lessons on what plants and animals need to survive.

generationData.instructions: For each item, write whether it is LIVING or NON-LIVING.
